misconceptions.description: Using a pie or doughnut chart to show change over time when the question is about a trend across an ordered axis
misconceptions.trigger: learner picks a pie chart to display values across months or years
misconceptions.feedback: Use a line chart for change over time. Reserve pie charts for parts of a single whole at one moment.

misconceptions.description: Starting a bar or column value axis above 0 so small differences look much larger than they are
misconceptions.trigger: learner leaves the value axis truncated on a bar or column chart
misconceptions.feedback: Start the value axis of a bar or column chart at 0 so bar heights stay proportional to the actual numbers.

misconceptions.description: Titling a chart with its topic or genre rather than the finding the reader should take away
misconceptions.trigger: learner labels a chart 'Sales Chart' or 'Figure 3' instead of stating the point
misconceptions.feedback: Write a claim-first title that states the finding, then let the chart serve as evidence for that one point.

misconceptions.description: Connecting unrelated categories with a line, implying a sequence that does not exist between separate groups
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses a line chart to compare discrete categories like separate stores
misconceptions.feedback: Compare discrete categories with a bar or column chart. Use a line only when the horizontal axis is an ordered sequence.
